REPUBLIC OF KENYA
IN THE EMPLOYMENT AND LABOUR RELATIONS COURT AT MOMBASA
CAUSE NO. E2207 OF 2025
BETWEEN
BRIAN OCHIENG OTIENO ........ CLAIMANT
AND
PWANI LOGISTICS LIMITED ........ RESPONDENT
JUDGMENT
Coram: Hon. Lady Justice F. A. Nduta-Mbaraka
Delivered on 5th June 2026
Background
1. The Claimant was employed by the Respondent as a forklift operator from 1st February 2019 at a gross monthly salary of KES 38,500. He was dismissed by a letter dated 14th March 2025 for alleged absence without leave.
2. He claims that the dismissal was unfair, that statutory deductions for the National Social Security Fund were made from his pay but not remitted for 22 months, and that he was not paid for accrued leave.
Evidence
3. The Claimant produced his payslips for 2023 and 2024, each of which shows a deduction of KES 2,160 described as 'NSSF Tier I and II'. He also produced a member statement from the Fund showing no contributions received between April 2023 and January 2025.
4. The Respondent's human resources officer conceded that the remittances were delayed because of cash-flow difficulties but said the arrears were being cleared in instalments.
Issues
5. The issues are whether the termination was fair, whether the Respondent breached its obligations in respect of social security contributions, and the remedies available.
Analysis
6. An employer is under a duty to register itself and its employees with the Fund, as provided in section 19 of the National Social Security Fund Act, 2013. Having deducted contributions from wages, the employer holds them for the Fund and may not apply them to its own purposes.
7. Section 22 of the same Act restricts what an employer may do with deductions made from an employee's wages. Retaining deducted contributions for 22 months is a clear breach of that provision.
8. On the termination, the Respondent did not issue a show-cause letter or hold a hearing. A termination without a fair procedure is unfair within the meaning of section 45 of the Employment Act, 2007, and I so find.
9. I have considered Otieno v Pwani Logistics, an earlier interlocutory ruling in this matter, and Kaluma v Bahari Freight Services Ltd [2022] KEELRC 90554 (KLR), which awarded compensation equivalent to six months' salary on similar facts.
Determination
10. The Claimant is awarded: (a) compensation equivalent to 6 months' gross salary, KES 231,000; (b) payment in lieu of 18 days' accrued leave, KES 23,100; and (c) an order directing the Respondent to remit all outstanding contributions, with penalties, to the Fund within 30 days and to file proof of remittance in court.
11. The Respondent shall pay the costs of the claim.
F. A. NDUTA-MBARAKA
JUDGE
